resources.string: Depends on the conductor material and insulation; take it from the standard or the cable manufacturer\'s datasheet.
Prospective short-circuit current at the installation point.
Optional: with the fault current, the time the cable can withstand it is calculated.
Isc at the start of the line
Three-phase short-circuit current at the panel the line leaves from.
Optional: without it, a zero-impedance upstream network is assumed.
Time for the protective device to clear the fault, from its curve.
Current the circuit draws in normal service.
Rated or set current of the breaker or fuse.
Optional: utility value at the MV connection point. Without it an infinite network is assumed.
Voltage between phase and neutral or phase and protective conductor.
Current that trips the device within the required time, for example 10 × In for curve C.
Minimum phase-neutral Isc at the end
Calculates the let-through energy (k²S²) a cable withstands in a short circuit; the protective device must let through less I²t than this.
Calculates the minimum cross-section that withstands a short-circuit current for the clearing time: S = I × √t / k.
Checks that the device rated current lies between the circuit design current and the conductor current rating.
Calculates the three-phase short-circuit current at a transformer\'s low-voltage terminals, including the medium-voltage network if known.
Calculates the three-phase short-circuit current at the end of a line from the one at the source panel.
Calculates the minimum short-circuit current (phase-to-neutral fault at the end of the line), which must trip the protective device.
Calculates the maximum line length so that a phase-to-neutral fault at the end reaches the device\'s magnetic trip current.
Impedance method with nominal voltage and the conductor at operating temperature; standard voltage and fault-temperature factors are not applied, so check with a margin.
